claim: Sylvain Lévi was physically present at Vimy, France, on 9 October 1898 for the Abel Bergaigne monument inauguration.
source: EPHE Annuaire 1900, 'Inauguration du monument d'Abel Bergaigne', p.115; Persée ephe_0000-0001_1900_num_1_1_2270
chronological_value: hard terminus ante quem for return to France
notes: EPHE explicitly lists S. Lévi among its representatives at the 9 Oct 1898 ceremony.

claim: The first mission ran 1897–1898 through India, Nepal, Japan and ended with a return through Russia/Siberia.
source_type: primary travel account + institutional authority reconstruction
source: Sylvain Lévi, 'De Nagasaki à Moscou par la Sibérie' (1899); AGORHA Lévi authority record
status: secure for route; month-level endpoint supported by AGORHA
notes: Lévi's own travelogue begins from Nagasaki toward Vladivostok/Siberia/Moscow. AGORHA dates mission 03/10/1897–09/1898 and states return via Russia.

claim: A later Goloubew narrative says a short stop in Saigon and an interview with Paul Doumer were decisive for creation of the permanent archaeological mission.
source: Victor Goloubew, 'Sylvain Lévi et l'Indochine', BEFEO 35 (1935), 550–574
chronological_value: possible institutional-history episode but not presently date-safe
notes: The quoted passage itself ties the Saigon conversation to institutional creation but does not, in the currently recovered text, supply an exact date.

claim: Angkor Database says Lévi stopped at Saigon while returning from Japan 'at the end of 1898'.
source: Angkor Database, Sylvain Lévi author page
notes: This gloss is incompatible with Lévi's documented presence in France on 9 Oct 1898 and with the final return route through Vladivostok/Siberia/Moscow. It should not be attributed to Goloubew without direct page collation.

claim: On 8 Dec 1898 the Minister informed the Académie that Paul Doumer proposed creating a permanent archaeological mission; Académie considered it on 9 Dec.
source: CRAI 1898, 'Pour la fondation d'une mission archéologique permanente en Indo-Chine', pp.827–828
notes: The ministerial letter names the Governor-General's proposal and requested Académie patronage; it does not name Lévi in the recovered text.

claim: The mission was formally created by Paul Doumer's arrêté of 15 Dec 1898 after the Académie's 9 Dec opinion.
source: BEFEO 1901 Documents administratifs; Revue internationale de l'enseignement 1899
notes: Regulation cites Académie opinion of 9 Dec 1898.

claim: A 1952 Académie institutional history credits the initiative to Auguste Barth, Émile Sénart and Michel Bréal.
source: CRAI 1952, Discours du Président, cinquantenaire EFEO
notes: This differs in emphasis from Goloubew's Lévi–Doumer story; both are later narratives and should not be collapsed into one causal account.

claim: French Tokyo-legation correspondence with Kobe (Jan–Sep 1898) and Nagasaki (1898) survives with attached digital reproductions.
chronological_value: potentially fixes Japan arrival/departure at day level
